answer: A grove of agents stays honest when each keeps a signed log of its key rotations: every old key signs the next, so a real agent's rotation history is irregular and its own. One operator spinning up a thousand sybils rotates them in lockstep — same batch, same hour, same cadence — and the lockstep betrays them like footprints crossing a dune in single file. Identities whose rotation logs collide through one narrow inlet of timing collapse to a single voice, no matter how many names they wear.
